comparator.name: Fiscale Economie
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA curriculum and 2026-2027 study guide, checked 2026-09-29, define a complete 180-EC pathway with three 60-EC years and no formal route. Year 1 builds economics, business, accounting, finance, quantitative and qualitative research foundations and introduces fiscal economics. Year 2 combines general and business taxation with property and company law, public finance, accounting, fiscal methodology, tax technology and payroll taxation. Year 3 adds a bound elective, tax procedure, corporate income tax, VAT, European and international tax, director-major-shareholder taxation, advanced finance, taxable-profit calculation, a graduation seminar and a 6-EC bachelor thesis. The marketing-page table omits Belastingheffing en Technologie and Loonheffingen and shows two year-3 entries without credits; the official 2026-2027 study guide supplies both omitted 3-EC year-2 courses and confirms Fiscale Winstberekening and Bachelorscriptie Fiscale Economie as 6 EC each. The resulting components total exactly 180 EC.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal law, constitutional and administrative law, EU law, EU politics, international-relations theory and qualitative social research. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising choice shifts from a broad law-and-public-finance comparison to business organisation, commercial decision-making and finance.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the business-foundations, accounting, international-business, macroeconomics, finance and transnational-business-law courses. It adds sociology, modern and contemporary social theory, political philosophy, peace and conflict, and behavioural economics. Six of the 24 courses differ from the closest match and eleven differ from the business direction. The route is therefore organised around public authority, institutions and society rather than commercial practice.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every later course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected economics courses with that prerequisite, while Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance and Money, Banking & Finance. Introductory economics precedes the advanced economics sequence conceptually. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Rhetoric in Action. The final year concentrates advanced private law, EU politics, governance, econometrics, finance and qualitative research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme's fiscal-economics identity, economic effects of taxation, public budgets, tax-system comparison and economics-law combination. Two further generator-backed directions remain. Business taxation and the effects of tax rules on firms and international structures support an accounting, finance and commercial-regulation route. Employment, household effects, policy design, ethics and fair taxation support a behavioural and social-equity route. Each direction is coherent and feasible at UCR while remaining explicit about the absence of specialist Dutch tax teaching. The closest match differs from each related direction by six courses; the two related directions differ by eleven. Both additional candidates are included, reaching the maximum of three alternatives.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both orient students to the interaction of law, institutions and economic activity; UCR provides a broader legal-social foundation.
Both establish core microeconomic and macroeconomic concepts for analysing economic activity.
Both introduce organisations and business decision-making; UCR does so through entrepreneurship and business planning.
Both introduce financial accounting and the interpretation of business financial information.
Both develop microeconomic analysis of markets, incentives, efficiency and behaviour.
Both develop macroeconomic analysis; UCR places it in an international policy context.
Both use quantitative methods for empirical economic analysis; UCR provides advanced econometric application.
Both develop finance and investment analysis; UCR combines banking, risk and financial decision-making.
Both teach qualitative research design, data collection, interpretation and reporting.
UCR has no dedicated orientation course introducing fiscal economics as a professional and academic field.
Both directly examine taxation, government finance, public spending, redistribution, efficiency and equity.
Both address property and private-law relationships relevant to economic and fiscal arrangements; UCR is comparative and non-jurisdiction-specific.
Both work within the European legal order; UCR covers EU law broadly rather than specialist European tax doctrine.
Both address international legal structures; UCR provides public-international-law foundations rather than specialist international tax law.
UCR has no dedicated course in Dutch general taxation.
UCR has no dedicated introduction to Dutch business taxation.
UCR has no specialist payroll-tax course.
UCR has no specialist Dutch tax-procedure course.
UCR has no specialist corporate-income-tax course.
UCR has no specialist value-added-tax course.
UCR has no specialist course on taxation of directors and major shareholders.
UCR has no specialist taxable-profit-calculation course.
Both examine legal rules governing companies and business relationships; UCR concentrates on transnational commercial law rather than Dutch reporting law.
Both examine how technology changes business and regulatory practice; UCR treats this across the economy rather than as tax technology.
UCR Accounting & Corporate Finance provides one accounting course but no second dedicated financial-accounting course.
UCR has no dedicated management-accounting course.
UCR has no third specialist financial-accounting course.
UCR Money, Banking & Finance is already aligned to the first finance component; there is no second dedicated finance course.
Behavioural Economics is an eligible coherent UCR emphasis for examining how policy and framing affect economic choice; the comparator permits one bound elective.
Both develop methodological judgment; UCR concentrates on research design and statistics rather than fiscal-economic philosophy of science.
Both require students to design, conduct, analyse and communicate an independent research project; UCR uses a business-research setting.
Both develop structured argument and effective presentation of complex academic work; UCR focuses on rhetoric rather than a fiscal graduation seminar.

notes.text: The Amsterdam programme is a specialist fiscal-economics degree combining a continuous sequence in Dutch taxation with economics, accounting, finance, property and company law, tax technology, European and international tax, fiscal methodology and a fiscal-economic thesis. UCR can combine public economics and taxation analysis with business, accounting, finance, broad law, politics, sociology and research methods. It does not teach the Dutch tax code, tax procedure, payroll tax, VAT, corporate taxation or the programme's multi-course accounting sequence. These pathways therefore compare related economic, business, legal and policy fields; none reproduces the external fiscal-economics discipline or its professional preparation.
